{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Devlog\PREJAM_PREP.md","content":"## Lessons from our previous project: tests and verification time (2026-11-10)
Source: two clean-up lots on Panthelia, our long-running Unreal project (UE 5.8, C++, about 7,300 automation tests), both closed on 2026-11-10. We carry over the rules, not the code. Each rule below cost us real hours once.

**What it cost.** In one week of November that project ran 1,333 headless test runs: 25.7 hours of machine time. 586 of those were mutation runs, each with two rebuilds. The pre-commit check took 334 s and the full suite about 15 minutes. After the two lots the same checks take about 90–105 s and about 6 minutes, with 37 pointless tests removed and everything else still green. None of the gain came from faster hardware.

### What to test in a 4-day jam
- **Test only logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing:** scoring, save and load, state machines, generators, math. Everything else is verified by playing the packaged build.
- **Keep the whole suite under 30 seconds of test time.** A check that takes minutes stops being run.
- **Do not write tests that are not tests.** We deleted 37: scans of the source text, checks that a field exists, and copies of constants, colors and UI positions. They fail when someone edits a number, not when the game breaks.
- **No registers.** No test catalog, no list of "known failures", no exclusion list. A run is green or red, and a red test is fixed or deleted the same day. Our registers needed a full suite run just to be refreshed, and a stale one blocked the check before Unreal even started.
- **Read a test's body before deleting it; the name can lie.** Six of the 37 looked like layout checks by name and tested real behavior. Two reviewers caught it and we restored them.
- **Name tests by tier, and never let a test name also be a folder.** If `Game.Save.Validate` exists and someone adds `Game.Save.Validate.Slots`, Unreal's Automation tree keeps the folder and silently stops running the first test. We had one that had stopped running and nobody saw it, because a test that does not run does not fail.

### A test needs an oracle that can fail
- For every test, ask: **what wrong implementation would still pass this?** If the answer is "most of them", the test is decoration.
- **One check per fixture when state latches.** We checked two things in one session of a tool whose "write detected" flag stays set until the session ends. When the first check tripped it, the second passed for the wrong reason. Each check now runs in its own session.
- **Mutate by risk, not per test.** Break the code on purpose in 1 to 3 places per change (a wrong result, a skipped guard, an unwanted side effect) and confirm the matching test fails for the expected reason. Mutating every test was our largest single source of runs.

### Measure before optimizing
- **Get three numbers first:** Editor boot, the sum of the test durations, and the wall time. What is left over is overhead. In our 225 s check they were 37 s, 114 s and 225 s, and even the 114 s was inflated: each duration included a wait for the next Editor frame. The real work of the tests was about 45 s.
- **Measure the whole, not the part.** Booting without the startup map cut one test family from 273 s to 31 s, so it looked like a pure win. On the full check it was slower (254 s against 225 s) and one test failed, because other tests relied on what the map kept loaded.
- **Timings vary from run to run.** The same code measured between 87 s and 108 s. Compare two paths on the same tree and report a range, not the best run.

### Where the time really went
- **The engine's `Automation RunTests` path spends about 4.5 Editor frames on every test.** The controller and the worker talk through messages, and the worker closes each test on the next frame. <#
Start-EditorMcp.ps1 - Abre el Editor UE 5.9 con el servidor MCP y espera a que este listo.
Uso:  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Start-EditorMcp.ps1 -Project D:\Jam\MiJuego\MiJuego.uproject -Port 8059
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Project,
    [int]$Port = 8059,
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 900
)
$exe = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path $exe)) { throw "No existe $exe" }
$name = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($Project)
$log = Join-Path (Split-Path $Project -Parent) "Saved\Logs\$name.log"
$start = Get-Date
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList "`"$Project`"", '-ModelContextProtocolStartServer', "-ModelContextProtocolPort=$Port" -PassThru
$t = 0
while ($t -lt $TimeoutSeconds) {
    Start-Sleep 5; $t += 5
    if ($p.HasExited) { Write-Host "El Editor se cerro (exit $($p.ExitCode))"; exit 1 }
    if ((Test-Path $log) -and (Get-Item $log).LastWriteTime -gt $start) {
        $m = Select-String $log -Pattern 'Starting MCP server|MCP server listener could not start' | Select-Object -Last 1
        if ($m) { Write-Host $m.Line; if ($m.Line -match 'could not') { exit 1 }; Write-Host "MCP listo en $t s (PID $($p.Id))"; exit 0 }
    }
}
Write-Host "Timeout esperando MCP ($TimeoutSeconds s). La primera apertura compila shaders: reintentar con mas tiempo."
exit 1

---
name: jam-autonomy-and-agent-routing
description: Glyphbound jam - never stop to ask; how to route work between Muse Spark, Claude subagents and Codex Sol 6.1
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Owner instructions given 2026-11-12 (Epic AI MegaJam, project Glyphbound), in their words summarized:

- **Do not stop to ask for authorizations, go-aheads or yes/no questions.** The owner is often away for hours; if the architect stops, the whole project stops. Find a simple solution and keep working.
- **Serial work (one code batch at a time) goes to Muse Spark via OpenCode.** Only one OpenCode session at a time.

<#
Build-Jam.ps1 - Compiles the Glyphbound C++ module (Editor target by default) and prints only what matters.
One build at a time per machine: do not run this while another build, a package or a test run is going.
The Editor must be closed (a full build cannot link while the Editor holds the DLLs).

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1                 # GlyphboundEditor Win64 Development
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound   # game target

Output: full log in Glyphbound/Saved/Logs/build_last.log; the console shows errors (first 60) and the result line.
Exit code: 0 = Result: Succeeded.
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$Target = 'GlyphboundEditor',
    [string]$Config = 'Development',
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$MaxErrors = 60
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$logDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Logs'
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($logDir)
$log = Join-Path $logDir 'build_last.log'
$bat = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat'
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
& cmd.exe /d /c "`"$bat`" $Target Win64 $Config -project=`"$Project`" -waitmutex > `"$log`" 2>&1"
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$sw.Stop()
$errors = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern '(: error |: fatal error |error LNK|Error: |ERROR: |UHT.*[Ee]rror)' | Select-Object -First $MaxErrors
if ($errors) { $errors | ForEach-Object { $_.Line.Trim() } }
$result = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern '^Result: ' | Select-Object -Last 1
if ($result) { Write-Host $result.Line } else { Write-Host "No 'Result:' line found (exit $code). See $log" }
Write-Host ("Build time: {0:N0} s  (exit {1})  log: {2}" -f $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, $code, $log)
exit $code

tool_input.content:
<#
Measure-EditorBoot.ps1 - Boots the Editor N times (Start-EditorMcp / Stop-EditorMcp) and reports
"Total Editor Startup Time" from the log plus the number of mounted plugins.
Timings vary from run to run: report the range, not the best run (Devlog/PREJAM_PREP.md).

Usage: powershell -File Tools/Jam/Measure-EditorBoot.ps1 -Label baseline -Runs 2
Appends one line per run to Glyphbound/Saved/Logs/boot_measurements.csv
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$Label = 'run',
    [int]$Runs = 2,
    [int]$Port = 8059
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$name = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($Project)
$log = Join-Path $projDir "Saved\Logs\$name.log"
$csv = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Logs\boot_measurements.csv'
if (-not (Test-Path $csv)) { 'utc,label,run,startup_seconds,mounted_plugins,mcp_ready' | Set-Content -Path $csv -Encoding ascii }
for ($i = 1; $i -le $Runs; $i++) {
    $out = & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Start-EditorMcp.ps1') -Project $Project -Port $Port
    $startCode = $LASTEXITCODE
    $ready = ($out | Select-String 'MCP listo en (\d+) s' | Select-Object -Last 1)
    $readyS = if ($ready) { $ready.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value } else { '' }
    # The startup line is written a moment after the MCP server starts: wait for it.
    $secs = ''
    for ($w = 0; $w -lt 30 -and -not $secs; $w++) {
        $m = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern 'Total Editor Startup Time, took ([\d\.]+)' | Select-Object -Last 1
        if ($m) { $secs = $m.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value } else { Start-Sleep 2 }
    }
    $mounted = @(Select-String -Path $log -Pattern 'Mounting (Engine|Project) plugin').Count
    Write-Host "[$Label] run ${i}: startup=$secs s, mounted plugins=$mounted, MCP ready=$readyS s (start exit $startCode)"
    ('{0},{1},{2},{3},{4},{5}' -f [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('o'), $Label, $i, $secs, $mounted, $readyS) | Add-Content -Path $csv -Encoding ascii
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Stop-EditorMcp.ps1') -Port $Port | Select-Object -Last 2
    Start-Sleep 3
}

{"file_path":"C:\GameJam\Design\ARCHITECTURE.md","content":"# Glyphbound: code architecture

> Written by the architect (Claude Code) on 2026-11-12. Source of truth for how the C++ is organized.
> Design lives in `Design/GDD.md`; this file says how the code implements it. Keep it short and current.

## Principles
1. **Data, not code.** Every gameplay number lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and is read through `UGBDataSubsystem`. Code never hardcodes damage, costs, speeds, durations, sizes or timings. The JSON ships as loose files, so numbers can be tuned in a packaged build with a text editor (`gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing).
2. **One stat system.** A number is a *named stat*: base value from data, then modifiers. `UGBStatsComponent` evaluates `(Base + adds) * multipliers` (or an override). Skill-tree nodes, armor, status effects, air passives and the weapon enchant are all just groups of modifiers with a source name. Nothing else changes numbers.
3. **One damage path.** Everything that hurts goes through `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Target, FGBDamageInfo)`. Shields, resistances, teams, on-hit effects and kill credit hook in there once.
4. **Spells are data + a behavior.** A spell is a `FGBSpellDefinition` (params with `Base/Min/Max/ScaledBy`) plus the class of an `AGBSpellActor` behavior. The QTE result (power, reach) scales the params tagged for it. A new spell that fits an existing behavior is a JSON entry, no code.
5. **Shared pieces.** One projectile (`AGBProjectile`) for staff bolts, spell projectiles, enemy shots and grenades. One status-effect component for slows, burns, potions and buffs. One interact interface for portals, chests, pickups and the seal.
6. **Text in git.** No binary assets are required to run: input actions, the test arena, placeholder shapes and placeholder pixel sprites are all built in C++ from text. `Content/` is ignored by git except `Content/Data/`.
7. **No GAS.** Unreal's Gameplay Ability System was considered and rejected for the jam: it needs a lot of boilerplate and asset setup, and the game's needs (costs, cooldowns, timed effects, stat upgrades) are covered by principles 2-4 in a few hundred lines we fully control.
8. **PIE is human-only.** Agents build, run the pure-logic tests and package; a person plays.

{"file_path":"C:\GameJam\Prompts\implementer_rules.md","content":"# Rules for every implementer on Glyphbound (read first)

You implement one part of **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter for the Epic AI MegaJam 2026, in **Unreal Engine 5.9.0**, C++. The architect (another agent) wrote the public headers; you write the implementation. Several implementers work **at the same time** on different folders, so the rules about file ownership matter.

## Read before writing
1. `C:\GameJam\Design\ARCHITECTURE.md` (the whole file, it is short).
2. `C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md`: the sections named in your task.

The header comments are the specification: implement what they say.

## File ownership
- You own ONLY the files listed in your task. Create the `.cpp` for each header you own, and new files inside your folders if you need them.
- **Never edit a file you do not own.** If you need something from another module that its header does not offer, code against what exists, and write the request in your final report.
- In headers you own you MAY add includes, private/protected members, helper methods and extra public methods. You MUST NOT remove, rename or change the signature of anything already public there: other implementers are calling it right now.
- Do not edit `Glyphbound.Build.cs`, `.uproject`, or `Config/`. Module dependencies available: Core, CoreUObject, Engine, InputCore, EnhancedInput, Json, JsonUtilities, AIModule, NavigationSystem, Slate, SlateCore, UMG. If you need another one, say so in your report.

## Hard rules
- **Do not build, do not run the Editor, do not run tests, do not commit, do not launch other agents.** The architect integrates and builds after everyone finishes. Write code that compiles: check every engine API you are not sure about in the engine source at `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source` (grep the header). UE 5.9 is newer than your training data; when in doubt, look.
- **No gameplay numbers in code.** Damage, costs, cooldowns, speeds, sizes, durations, timings and counts come from the JSON data through `UGBDataSubsystem` and `UGBStatsComponent` (stat names in `Core/GBStatNames.h`). If you need a number that has no stat yet, add a named constant `inline const FName` in a header YOU own (same style as `GBStatNames.h`), read it from the data with a sensible default, put its value in your JSON file, and list it in your report. Layout pixels and pure visual offsets may be code constants.
- Everything must work when a JSON entry is missing: use the default argument, log a warning with `UE_LOG(LogGB, Warning, ...)`, never crash, never divide by zero.
- No binary assets. 3D placeholders: `GBPlaceholder::SetupShape` (engine basic shapes). Pixel-art placeholders: `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary` (sprites described as text in `Sprites.json`). Art rule (GDD 3): medieval and magic things are pixel-art sprites; cyberpunk things are 3D.
- No custom collision channels or profiles that need config: use the engine's default channels and filter by team in code (`UGBCombatLibrary::AreHostile`).
- Do not keep pointers to definitions (`FGBSpellDefinition*`...) across frames; keep the id.
- A class member must never be named `Cast` (it hides the engine's `Cast<T>()`).
- All on-screen text in English. Comments in English, and only where they explain a decision or a non-obvious rule. ASCII only.
- Includes are relative to the module root: `#include "Stats/GBStatsComponent.h"`. Every `.cpp` includes its own header first. Every header with reflected types includes its `.generated.h` last.
- Keep it simple. This is a 4-day jam: clear, short code that works beats clever code. No  ...[recortado: 5165 chars]

{"file_path":"C:\GameJam\Devlog\days\2026-11-12.md","content":"# Day 1: 2026-11-12

> Architect's entry, written by the AI architect (Claude Code) as the day went. A person on the team reviews it and adds the human side (play-test notes, screenshots) starting from `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.

## Summary in 3 lines
- The owner directed, the AI architect decided every technical point alone and built the project "Glyphbound" from an empty folder: UE 5.9.0, C++, no template gameplay code.
- The whole code structure of the game was laid out in one pass: the architect wrote the header contracts, then ten AI implementers filled them in parallel, and one integration pass made it build.
- TODO at close: result of the build, tests, package and the first human play-test.

## Goal of the day vs. result
| Goal | Result | Evidence (commit, screenshot, clip) |
|---|---|---|
| Create the UE 5.9.0 project with unused plugins off, measure Editor boot before and after | Done. See "Numbers" below | commit `8034a7c` |
| First-person controller (move, jump, double jump, dash) | TODO | |

Periodic damage from status effects must NOT re-apply on-hit effects (the effect component passes OnHitEffect = NAME_None).
   - `DealRadialDamage`: `UWorld::OverlapMultiByObjectType` with a sphere for Pawn + WorldDynamic object types, unique actors, skip `IgnoreActors`, skip actors without attributes, skip non-hostile to the instigator; per target fill HitLocation (target location) and HitDirection (from Origin); with falloff scale Amount by 1 - dist/Radius (clamped). {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\ARCHITECTURE.md","content":"# Glyphbound: code architecture

> Written by the architect (Claude Code) on 2026-11-12. Source of truth for how the C++ is organized.
> Design lives in `Design/GDD.md`; this file says how the code implements it. Keep it short and current.

## Principles
1. **Data, not code.** Every gameplay number lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and is read through `UGBDataSubsystem`. Code never hardcodes damage, costs, speeds, durations, sizes or timings. The JSON ships as loose files, so numbers can be tuned in a packaged build with a text editor (`gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing).
2. **One stat system.** A number is a *named stat*: base value from data, then modifiers. `UGBStatsComponent` evaluates `(Base + adds) * multipliers` (or an override). Skill-tree nodes, armor, status effects, air passives and the weapon enchant are all just groups of modifiers with a source name. Nothing else changes numbers.
3. **One damage path.** Everything that hurts goes through `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Target, FGBDamageInfo)`. Shields, resistances, teams, on-hit effects and kill credit hook in there once.
4. **Spells are data + a behavior.** A spell is a `FGBSpellDefinition` (params with `Base/Min/Max/ScaledBy`) plus the class of an `AGBSpellActor` behavior. The QTE result (power, reach) scales the params tagged for it. A new spell that fits an existing behavior is a JSON entry, no code.
5. **Shared pieces.** One projectile (`AGBProjectile`) for staff bolts, spell projectiles, enemy shots and grenades. One status-effect component for slows, burns, potions and buffs. One interact interface for portals, chests, pickups and the seal.
6. **Text in git.** No binary assets are required to run: input actions, the test arena, placeholder shapes and placeholder pixel sprites are all built in C++ from text. `Content/` is ignored by git except `Content/Data/`.
7. **No GAS.** Unreal's Gameplay Ability System was considered and rejected for the jam: it needs a lot of boilerplate and asset setup, and the game's needs (costs, cooldowns, timed effects, stat upgrades) are covered by principles 2-4 in a few hundred lines we fully control.
8. **PIE is human-only.** Agents build, run the pure-logic tests and package; a person plays.

## Module layout (`Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound`, one runtime module, prefix `GB`)
Includes are relative to the module root: `#include "Stats/GBStatsComponent.h"`.

| Folder | What | Key types |

| `Core/` | Shared enums, stat names, placeholders, game mode | `GBTypes.h`, `GBStatNames.h`, `GBPlaceholder.h`, `AGBGameMode`, `UGBGameInstance` |

**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).

Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.

### Flow
1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).

   - Gamepad: the right stick.

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md","content":"## 3. Art rule (never broken)
- **Everything medieval, wizards and magic is pixel art (2D).**
- **Everything cyberpunk and futuristic is 3D.**
- **The rule follows the object, not the era.** A 3D gun stays 3D in the past; a pixel-art fireball stays pixel art in the future.
- **Characters take the style of the world they belong to.** An orc of the castle is a classic pixel-art fantasy orc (80s, 90s, early 2000s games). An orc of the future is a 3D, heavily armored sci-fi orc. They are different enemies, not the same orc in two styles.
- **The player is a medieval mage, so the player is always pixel art, hands included.** In first person, the hands are always pixel art, even when they hold a 3D gun.
- No exceptions.

### The pixel-art look
- **Visual reference:** retro first-person fantasy shooters with modern lighting (the owner's reference: *Wizordum*). Reference only, nothing copied.
- **Pixel-art environments are 3D geometry with low-resolution pixel textures** (nearest filtering, no smoothing), not flat 2D.
- **Pixel-art characters are sprites that always face the camera.** Target: **8 view angles**; fewer if time runs short.
- **Headshots on sprites:** the head is the top part of the sprite.

## 4. World and travel
- **One map, two times** (past and future). The player travels between them **only through predefined portals** placed on the map.
- **Era-gated zones:** some zones are reachable in one era and not in the other.

- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.
- **Era travel restores everything** (health, mana, ammo), a bit like the rest points of classic action RPGs. Portals are the safe points of the map.

- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).

- The player is a **mage** who travels to the castle out of **curiosity**: he had heard it was a mysterious place.
- On reaching the **seal** in the castle he is **trapped** and thrown into the future.
- In the future he hears **a woman's voice asking for help**. That voice is his reason to fix the problem.
- **The twist:** the voice is **not the Valkyrie**. It is **the Entity**, the true final boss, pretending to be her.

- **What the player does:** defeats the Valkyrie in both eras, gathers what is needed, and opens the portal: **exactly the Entity's plan**. The player walks in with the body it wants to possess. The only thing the Entity did not plan for: **the player beats it**.
- Cutscenes: **few and short**, each one written for its situation.

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md","content":"## 0. Baseline
At its core this is a **classic first-person RPG plus a classic first-person shooter**. Anything not stated here behaves as players expect from those two genres (magazines and reload, ammo pickups, standard shooter gamepad layout, etc.). This document only lists what is specific to our game.

## 0.1 Technical direction
- **Engine:** Unreal Engine 5.9.0, pinned until submission. **Single player only.**
- **Architect autonomy:** nobody on the team is a programmer. **Every technical and engineering decision is the architect's**, taken without asking the owner: code architecture, C++ vs. Blueprints, plugins, tools, data formats, optimization. Decide, build, and log the decision and its reason in the dev log. When a design detail is missing, pick a reasonable provisional value, mark it provisional here, and keep going; ask the owner only when the game's vision would change.
- **Time first:** iteration speed matters more than elegance. Unused plugins off, Live Coding for `.cpp` changes, only the touched tests on each change, the full suite (under 30 s) once before the daily package. Rules in `CLAUDE.md` ("Tiempo de iteración").
- **Code:** C++ suggested for the core systems (AI agents handle code better than Blueprint graphs), with data assets / data tables for tuning. Final call: the architect.
- **Placeholders first:** pixel art and 3D models are made by other team members on machines on the local network. **The architect never waits for art:** it uses quickly generated placeholders and swaps them later.
- **Placeholder numbers:** the architect puts provisional values (damage, mana, cooldowns, QTE length and time limit…) in data tables; the owner tunes them later.
- **PIE is human-only:** Play In Editor is always run by a person. AI agents do not run PIE; they compile, package and run tests, then ask a human to play-test. (Also in `CLAUDE.md`.)
- **Era travel:** a fade with an effect when crossing a portal; the transition hides loading the other era's version of the map.
- **Saving:** checkpoints only. No save to disk between sessions.
- **Size:** the jam page says "keep it under 1 GB" for desktop zips, but **bigger builds are allowed** if uploaded with butler (installed on CENTRAL) or Blendo Itch Uploader. The Official Rules PDF sets no size limit. So 1 GB is a target, not a hard limit.
- **NVIDIA RTX Award:** we intend to compete. It is the "best Render Royalty entry built in Unreal Engine" that uses at least one of: an NvRTX feature (RTX Mega Geometry, RTX Direct Illumination, ReSTIR GI, ReSTIR PT path tracing, LSS Hair), **DLSS 4.5 (Unreal Engine)**, or NVIDIA ACE; plus the NVIDIA questions at submission and listing the tool in "Tools you used".
- **Modifier rule (Official Rules §10):** a team can win **only one modifier** (Glass Box, Render Royalty, Best Team…) unless no other eligible winner remains. We still enter all that apply.

## 1. One-line pitch
A fast first-person **shooter/RPG hybrid**: the player, a medieval mage, jumps through fixed portals between a **pixel-art medieval past** full of magic and a **3D cyberpunk future** full of guns, on the same map in two times, and wins by **mixing spells and firearms** rather than sticking to one style.

Working title: **TBD**. Project code name: **Glyphbound**.

## 2. Pillars
1. **Two eras, one fight.** Past = magic, pixel art. Future = guns, 3D cyberpunk. Both feed the same character.
2. **Combos over specialization.** Spells and guns can be used in both eras, and the game rewards combining them. Weapon and spell mechanics have synergies.
3. **Fast and dynamic combat:** spells, ranged spells, shooting, and melee once the elemental sword is unlocked.
4. **Magic feels crafted, not triggered:** casting uses a two-part slowed-time quick-time event that scales the spell (see §7).

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md","content":"## 10. Enemies and encounters
- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
- **The true final boss.**
- Known enemies: **orcs** (past) and **armed orcs** (future). Other types and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).
- Enemies **drop ammo** on the floor.
- **Enemies do not respawn.** A cleared zone stays cleared, also after era travel.

### Death and difficulty
- On death the player **returns to the last checkpoint**. Checkpoints are **automatic**.
- **Difficulty: hard**, the only one for now. A separate normal mode is possible later (for example, the spell QTE only in hard); out of scope until the owner says otherwise.
- No target length: we build as much as the time allows.

## 11. Bosses and endgame
**The Valkyrie (two bosses, one in each era).**
- **Past:** trapped inside magic runes in the medieval castle.
- **Future:** trapped in a cryogenic tube.
- The player must **free her and defeat her in both eras.**

Rewards:
| Defeated in | Drops |
|---|---|
| Past (castle) | **Elemental stones/gems** |
| Future | **A weapon hilt** |
| Both fights | One **quest item** each (what they are: **TBD**) |

- **Elemental sword:** in the inventory, the player combines the hilt with a gem and gets an elemental sword that comes out of the hilt. The player can switch the sword to the other elements from the inventory. It is the only melee weapon. The weapon enchant does not apply to it.
  - Art (§3): the **hilt is 3D** (it comes from the future), the **blade is pixel art** (it is magic).
  - HUD: **medieval** (provisional).
- **Final portal:** combining the two quest items opens a portal to a separate map, a dimension between space and time, where the player fights the **true final boss**.
- **True final boss: the Entity** (story in §4). A **mix of both art styles**, which fits what it is (suggestion, not decided: the AI half in 3D, the ghost half in pixel art). Undecided how: two phases with different styles, or one character in both styles at once, or something else (**TBD**).
- This happens in mid/late game.

## 12. Inventory
Needed for: consumables, equipping/unequipping spells, choosing the enchant element, combining hilt + gem, switching the sword's element, combining the two quest items. Layout and limits **TBD**.

## 13. UI: two styles
The UI changes with what the player holds:

| Holding | HUD style |
|---|---|
| Staff (magic) | **1990s first-person RPG** |
| Gun | **Modern cyberpunk** |
| Elemental sword | Medieval / 90s RPG (provisional) |

- **Skill trees** follow the same split: the spell tree has its own 90s-RPG look, the weapon tree its own cyberpunk look.
- The HUD switches when the player switches weapon. The inventory's look is **TBD**.

## 14. Theme fit (DIRECTOR'S CUT)
Our reading (owner, 2026-11-12): the theme is effectively **open**; what the organizers ask for is a game with an **author's signature**, a personal vision. We answer it with the game's own identity:
- the hard art split (pixel-art magic vs. 3D cyberpunk) that follows each object and never breaks, with a pixel-art mage holding 3D guns;
- a UI that also changes style with what the player holds;
- magic that has to be performed (the QTE) rather than triggered;
- a combat style that rewards mixing the two eras.

The dev log shows the directing side too: how we direct the AI agents, and every scope decision ("what made the final cut"). Any feature we drop gets logged as a cut, with the reason.

| Day | Target |

## 10. Enemies and encounters
- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
- **The true final boss.**
- Known enemies: **orcs** (past) and **armed orcs** (future). Other types and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).
- Enemies **drop ammo** on the floor.
- **Enemies do not respawn.** A cleared zone stays cleared, also after era travel.

### Death and difficulty
- On death the player **returns to the last checkpoint**. Checkpoints are **automatic**.
- **Difficulty: hard**, the only one for now. A separate normal mode is possible later (for example, the spell QTE only in hard); out of scope until the owner says otherwise.
- No target length: we build as much as the time allows.

<#
Test-Jam.ps1 - Runs the pure-logic automation tests headless and decides pass/fail from the report.
Rules (Devlog/PREJAM_PREP.md, "Lessons from our previous project"):
  - anchored filters: start with ^ and end with a dot; join several with + (one Editor boot);
  - every run writes to its own new folder; the verdict comes from the report, not only the exit code;
  - a run with fewer tests than -MinTests is a failure (guards against a typo in the filter);
  - one build or test run at a time per machine; the Editor must be closed.

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1                              # the whole suite: ^Glyphbound.
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -Filter '^Glyphbound.QTE.'   # only what was touched
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -Filter '^Glyphbound.QTE.+^Glyphbound.Spells.'
Exit code: 0 = every selected test passed and at least MinTests ran.
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$Filter = '^Glyphbound.',
    [int]$MinTests = 1,
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 600
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$stamp = [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyyMMdd-HHmmss')
$runDir = Join-Path $projDir "Saved\TestRuns\$stamp"
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($runDir)
$log = Join-Path $runDir 'editor.log'
$exe = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe'
$argList = @(
    "`"$Project`"",
    "-ExecCmds=`"Automation RunTests $Filter; Quit`"",
    '-TestExit="Automation Test Queue Empty"',
    "-ReportExportPath=`"$runDir`"",
    "-abslog=`"$log`"",
    '-unattended', '-nopause', '-nosplash', '-NullRHI', '-nosound', '-nocrashreports'
)
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $argList -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden
if (-not $p.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)) {
    Write-Host "TIMEOUT after $TimeoutSeconds s. The Editor process (PID $($p.Id)) is still running; log: $log"
    exit 3
}
$sw.Stop()
$index = Join-Path $runDir 'index.json'
if (-not (Test-Path $index)) {
    Write-Host "FAIL: no report was written (exit $($p.ExitCode)). Did the module load? Log: $log"
    Select-String -Path $log -Pattern 'Error:|error:|No automation tests matched' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 15 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
    exit 2
}
$report = Get-Content $index -Raw -Encoding UTF8 | ConvertFrom-Json
$tests = @($report.tests)
$failed = @($tests | Where-Object { $_.state -ne 'Success' })
$testSeconds = 0.0
foreach ($t in $tests) { $testSeconds += [double]$t.duration }
foreach ($t in $failed) {
    Write-Host "FAILED: $($t.fullTestPath) [$($t.state)]"
    foreach ($e in @($t.entries)) { if ($e.event.type -eq 'Error') { Write-Host "   $($e.event.message)" } }
}
$ensures = @(Select-String -Path $log -Pattern 'Ensure condition failed' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Count
Write-Host ("Tests: {0} run, {1} failed, test time {2:N2} s, wall time {3:N0} s, ensures in log: {4}" -f $tests.Count, $failed.Count, $testSeconds, $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, $ensures)
Write-Host "Report: $runDir"
if ($tests.Count -lt $MinTests) { Write-Host "FAIL: only $($tests.Count) tests ran, expected at least $MinTests (check the filter)."; exit 4 }
if ($failed.Count -gt 0) { exit 1 }
exit 0

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md","content":"## 0. Baseline
At its core this is a **classic first-person RPG plus a classic first-person shooter**. Anything not stated here behaves as players expect from those two genres (magazines and reload, ammo pickups, standard shooter gamepad layout, etc.). This document only lists what is specific to our game.

## 0.1 Technical direction
- **Engine:** Unreal Engine 5.9.0, pinned until submission. **Single player only.**
- **Architect autonomy:** nobody on the team is a programmer. **Every technical and engineering decision is the architect's**, taken without asking the owner: code architecture, C++ vs. Blueprints, plugins, tools, data formats, optimization. Decide, build, and log the decision and its reason in the dev log. When a design detail is missing, pick a reasonable provisional value, mark it provisional here, and keep going; ask the owner only when the game's vision would change.
- **Time first:** iteration speed matters more than elegance. Unused plugins off, Live Coding for `.cpp` changes, only the touched tests on each change, the full suite (under 30 s) once before the daily package. Rules in `CLAUDE.md` ("Tiempo de iteración").
- **Code:** C++ suggested for the core systems (AI agents handle code better than Blueprint graphs), with data assets / data tables for tuning. Final call: the architect.
- **Placeholders first:** pixel art and 3D models are made by other team members on machines on the local network. **The architect never waits for art:** it uses quickly generated placeholders and swaps them later.
- **Placeholder numbers:** the architect puts provisional values (damage, mana, cooldowns, QTE length and time limit…) in data tables; the owner tunes them later.
- **PIE is human-only:** Play In Editor is always run by a person. AI agents do not run PIE; they compile, package and run tests, then ask a human to play-test. (Also in `CLAUDE.md`.)
- **Era travel:** a fade with an effect when crossing a portal; the transition hides loading the other era's version of the map.
- **Saving:** checkpoints only. No save to disk between sessions.
- **Size:** the jam page says "keep it under 1 GB" for desktop zips, but **bigger builds are allowed** if uploaded with butler (installed on CENTRAL) or Blendo Itch Uploader. The Official Rules PDF sets no size limit. So 1 GB is a target, not a hard limit.
- **NVIDIA RTX Award:** we intend to compete. It is the "best Render Royalty entry built in Unreal Engine" that uses at least one of: an NvRTX feature (RTX Mega Geometry, RTX Direct Illumination, ReSTIR GI, ReSTIR PT path tracing, LSS Hair), **DLSS 4.5 (Unreal Engine)**, or NVIDIA ACE; plus the NVIDIA questions at submission and listing the tool in "Tools you used".
- **Modifier rule (Official Rules §10):** a team can win **only one modifier** (Glass Box, Render Royalty, Best Team…) unless no other eligible winner remains. We still enter all that apply.

## 1. One-line pitch
A fast first-person **shooter/RPG hybrid**: the player, a medieval mage, jumps through fixed portals between a **pixel-art medieval past** full of magic and a **3D cyberpunk future** full of guns, on the same map in two times, and wins by **mixing spells and firearms** rather than sticking to one style.

Working title: **TBD**. Project code name: **Glyphbound**.

3. **Fast and dynamic combat:** spells, ranged spells, shooting, and melee once the elemental sword is unlocked.
4. **Magic feels crafted, not triggered:** casting uses a two-part slowed-time quick-time event that scales the spell (see §7).

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md","content":"## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).

Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.

### Flow
1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
   - Gamepad: the right stick.
4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.

### Grading and cost
- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.

### What each part scales
| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
|---|---|---|
| Fireball | Damage | Blast radius / range |
| Ice wall | Duration and wall health | Width and height |
| Ice shield | Duration and block effectiveness (which part scales which: **TBD**) | |
| Others | **TBD**, following the same idea: part 1 = strength, part 2 = size/area/range |

### Requirements for the architect
- **Every spell parameter is data, not code**, and every one can be tagged as scaled by part 1, part 2, or neither. Each spell defines its own min/max per parameter.
- The **time-slow amount is configurable** and can be modified by gear (e.g. some armor). Armor/gear as a system is otherwise **TBD**.
- **The camera is locked during the QTE** (the mouse / right stick draws the gesture).
- **The player keeps moving during the QTE, in the direction they were already moving** (the movement keys are busy with part 1, so the last movement input is held).
- **QTE time limit: 3 seconds** for the **whole QTE** (both parts together), in real time (provisional value in data).

## 8. Weapons and items

### Held slots
- The player carries **one gun and one staff.** Never two guns or two staffs.
- Once obtained, the **elemental sword is a special third slot.**
- Switch with the **mouse wheel or Alt**; on gamepad, with a **D-pad arrow** (which one: **TBD**).
- Staff in hand: basic magic attack + the 5 spells. Gun in hand: shoot + aim + reload + the enchant.

### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
- Staffs are found in **chests** around the map.
- Staff list and what each basic attack does: **TBD**.

### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
- The **first gun** is dropped by one of the first armed orcs in the future (§4). The **shotgun and the rifle** are dropped later by enemies, picked up from the floor.
- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
- **Magazines and reload**, like any shooter.
- **Ammo works like classic tactical shooters:** each gun has a fixed number of spare magazines, and each magazine a fixed number of bullets.
- **All ammo refills completely every time the player travels between eras.**
- Between refills, ammo is **picked up from the floor** where enemies drop it.
- Level design keeps ammo tight: never infinite, never starving.
- **Electric grenade** (throwable).

### Armor
- Found in **chests**, rarely.
- **One armor slot = one full armor.** No separate helmet, arms or chest pieces.
- Known effect: some armor changes the QTE time-slow amount (§7). Other stats: **TBD**.

# Task: make Glyphbound build and pass its tests (integration pass)

You are the integration implementer for **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++, project in `Glyphbound/`). Ten implementers wrote the code of the module `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound` in parallel, each in its own folder, against public headers written by the architect. **Nobody has compiled it yet.** Your job is to make it compile, link and pass the tests, changing as little as possible.

## Read first
1. `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` (short).
2. `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` (the rules the implementers followed; the "Hard rules" also apply to you, except that you DO build and run tests).
3. `Prompts/day1_integration_notes.md` (the implementers' own reports: API they added, things they could not verify, requests between modules). Start with the risks they listed.

## Loop
1. Build: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -MaxErrors 80`
   - It prints the errors and `Result: Succeeded` or `Result: Failed`. The full log is `Glyphbound/Saved/Logs/build_last.log`.
   - One build at a time. Never start a second build while one is running. Do not open the Unreal Editor.
2. Fix the errors, starting with the first ones (header and UHT errors cause cascades). Then build again.
3. When the build says `Result: Succeeded`, run the tests:
   `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 12`
   Fix what fails (see "Tests" below), rebuild, and repeat until both are green.

## How to fix
- The header comments written by the architect are the specification. When two files disagree, make the code match the header comment; when a header is plainly wrong for the engine (a signature that does not exist in UE 5.9), fix the header and every caller.
- Check engine APIs in the engine source before guessing: `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source` and `...\Engine\Plugins`. UE 5.9 is newer than your training data.
- Smallest change that is correct. Do not rewrite a file that only has a few errors. Do not reformat.
- **Never make an error disappear by deleting behavior**: no emptied function bodies, no commented-out features, no `#if 0`. If something truly cannot work, leave the smallest stub that compiles and report it clearly.
- Missing includes and forward declarations are the most likely errors; unresolved externals mean a function was declared in a header and never written (write it, following the header comment) or a module is missing from `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Glyphbound.Build.cs` (you may add engine modules there).
- No gameplay numbers in code: if you must add a number, it goes in the JSON under `Glyphbound/Content/Data` with a named stat.
- Keep the JSON files valid JSON. If you touch one, re-read it whole afterwards.

## Tests
- A failing test means the code or the test is wrong. Read both. Fix the code when the code breaks the rule in the header comment; fix the test only when the test contradicts the header comment, and say so in your report.
- Never delete or skip a test to get a green run. Never weaken an assertion until it passes.

## Do not
- Do not commit, push, or touch git history.
- Do not edit files outside `Glyphbound/Source`, `Glyphbound/Content/Data` and `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Glyphbound.Build.cs`.
- Do not launch other agents, the Editor, or the game.

## Final report (plain text)
1. Final state: build result line and the tests summary line, copied verbatim.
2. What you fixed, grouped by kind (missing includes, wrong engine API, mismatched signatures between modules, unresolved externals, logic bugs found by tests), with file names.
3. Anything you stubbed or could not make work.
4. Anything that looks wrong at runtime even though it compiles (things a human should check while playing).

{"stdout":"# Jam dev log (goal: the Glass Box prize for the best dev log)

Everything any agent or person does on the project must be recorded here. If it is not in the dev log, it did not happen as far as the judges are concerned.

**Language:** the Official Rules (7(i)) require every part of the submission in English, and that includes the published dev log. Write `days/*.md`, `media/` captions and `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` in English. Raw logs (`raw/`) and the team's prompts to agents can be in any language. When a day entry quotes a prompt written in Spanish, include the original and an English translation.

## Layout

```
Devlog/
  README.md                  this file (the rules)
  TEMPLATE_DAY.md            template for the daily entry
  PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md     what was prepared BEFORE Nov 12 (the jam requires declaring it)
  PREJAM_PREP.md             full pre-jam log: timeline, tests, tools evaluated, rules read
  raw/<MACHINE>/             raw automatic logs (NEVER published as they are)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/claude-<session>.jsonl      every Claude Code event (hook)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/transcripts/<session>.jsonl full transcript of each session
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents.jsonl                every run of an external agent
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
```

## Rules for everyone (people and agents)

1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
   - **Cursor** (the art LAPTOP, which has no repo) is logged by user-level Cursor hooks instead: `Tools/Devlog/Install-CursorHooks.ps1` installs `cursor-devlog-hook.ps1`, which writes `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\cursor-<conversation>.jsonl` (plus transcripts). `Register-LaptopDevlogTasks.ps1` copies that folder every 10 minutes to `Incoming\LAPTOP\_devlog_raw` on CENTRAL, and CENTRAL's `JamDevlogImport` task (`Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1`) moves it into `Devlog/raw/`, where `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads it.
3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.

- **QTE time limit: 3 seconds** for the **whole QTE** (both parts together), in real time (provisional value in data).

## 8. Weapons and items

### Held slots
- The player carries **one gun and one staff.** Never two guns or two staffs.
- Once obtained, the **elemental sword is a special third slot.**
- Switch with the **mouse wheel or Alt**; on gamepad, with a **D-pad arrow** (which one: **TBD**).
- Staff in hand: basic magic attack + the 5 spells. Gun in hand: shoot + aim + reload + the enchant.

### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
- Staffs are found in **chests** around the map.
- Staff list and what each basic attack does: **TBD**.

### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
- The **first gun** is dropped by one of the first armed orcs in the future (§4). The **shotgun and the rifle** are dropped later by enemies, picked up from the floor.
- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
- **Magazines and reload**, like any shooter.
- **Ammo works like classic tactical shooters:** each gun has a fixed number of spare magazines, and each magazine a fixed number of bullets.
- **All ammo refills completely every time the player travels between eras.**
- Between refills, ammo is **picked up from the floor** where enemies drop it.
- Level design keeps ammo tight: never infinite, never starving.
- **Electric grenade** (throwable).

### Armor
- Found in **chests**, rarely.
- **One armor slot = one full armor.** No separate helmet, arms or chest pieces.
- Known effect: some armor changes the QTE time-slow amount (§7). Other stats: **TBD**.

### Chests
- Contain **staffs**, and rarely **armor**. Other contents: **TBD**.

### Melee
- **No melee before the elemental sword** (§11).

### Consumables
| Item | Era | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Health potion | Past | Heals a set amount **over time** |
| Mana potion | Past | Restores a set amount of mana **over time** |
| Electric grenade | Future | Throwable, electric damage |
| Health injection | Future | Heals **instantly**, but less than the potion |

### Synergies
Weapon mechanics and spell mechanics combine. The weapon enchant (§6) is the first confirmed one. Other synergies (e.g. shooting through a fire wall, electric grenade on an ice floor) are **TBD**.

## 9. Controls

| Action | Keyboard & mouse | Gamepad |

| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | R2 / RT |

| Reload (gun) | R | Standard shooter layout |

| Jump | Space | Cross (A) |

| Skill trees | K (also a tab inside the inventory) | From the inventory |

- defeating each **boss**;
  - **clearing a wave** of enemies.

## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.

| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS) |
| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
| **Ice** | Ice shield (held block, like a first-person RPG shield, but with a cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |

### Spell loadout
- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall.

### Learning the other spells: elemental zones
- The **medieval castle** has **elemental zones**, one per element.
- Each zone has a **challenge**: a wave, a sub-boss or a boss.
- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
- **Air passives** are learned the same way, in the air zone.
- The spell tree then upgrades what the player knows.
- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
- Keys: see §9.

### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
- **Only usable with a gun in hand** (it enchants the gun).
- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.

### General
- Spells cost **mana**.
- **Health and mana regenerate on their own** (potions and the injection speed it up). **No stamina.**

- Source/Glyphbound/Tests/GBQTETests.cpp (new). Six tests:

  - `Glyphbound.QTE.GestureShort`

- Content/Data/QTE.json (new).

- `namespace GBQTEStat` with five FName constants: `QTE.GestureMinScore`, `QTE.GestureMinLength`, `QTE.GestureIdleSubmitTime`, `QTE.LineSubmitLengthMult`, `QTE.StickGestureScale`.
- `const FGBQTEResult& GetLastResult() const`
- `float GetStickGestureScale() const`. The player character should send `RightStick * GetStickGestureScale() * real delta seconds` to `HandleGestureInput`.
- Also added (protected): `ReadStat`, `BuildConfig`, `LastResult`, `GestureIdleSubmitTime`, `LineSubmitLengthMult`.

3. Requests for other modules
- Player (AGBPlayerCharacter): scale right-stick input by `QTE->GetStickGestureScale()` times `FApp::GetDeltaTime()`. Use the undilated delta, because the world runs at 0.1 speed during the QTE. Mouse deltas go in as raw pixels.
- Core: the code uses `LogGB`. It is declared in GBTypes.h, but some Core cpp must have `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY(LogGB)`, or linking fails.

4. Design values I invented (please mark them provisional)
- `QTE.GestureMinScore` 0.35 and `QTE.GestureMinLength` 120 px (same as the header defaults).
- `QTE.GestureIdleSubmitTime` 0.25 real seconds.
- `QTE.LineSubmitLengthMult` 2.5. The task gave 2.5 x GestureMinLength; I moved it into data so it is not a number in code.
- `QTE.StickGestureScale` 600 px per second at full tilt.
- Circle closure rule: closure = 1 - (gap between start and end) / (diagonal of the stroke's bounding box), clamped to 0..1. A 3/4 circle scores about 0.37.
- Success with zero steps: if SequenceLength and GestureCount are both 0, the result is `bSuccess = true`, since no step was missed. Read literally, the spec would make that setup always fail.

5. Risks and behavior notes
- Real time comes from `FApp::GetDeltaTime()`. The component only ticks while the game is not paused, so a pause does not eat QTE time.
- The component's tick is off until StartQTE and is turned off again in Finish (`bCanEverTick = true`, `bStartWithTickEnabled = false`). This is cheaper than ticking always.
- Finish always sets global time dilation back to 1. If anything else sets dilation, it gets overwritten.
- EndPlay restores dilation but does not fire the delegate.
- CancelQTE fires the delegate. Unfinished steps count as missed.
- The callback gets a local copy of the result, so it is safe to start a new QTE from inside it.
- Every value is read through `UGBStatsComponent::Evaluate`, the thresholds included, so gear can change any of them. ## SPELLS (spellbook, cast resolution, 8 behaviors)
- Added: `AGBSpellActor::StartSpell()` (protected virtual run once after InitSpell and BeginPlay) and helper methods; `GBSpellParam` constants (SpriteSize, Distance, ExplosionRadius, ExplosionFalloff, Pierce, VisualScale, Blocking, ArmTime, TriggerRadius, BlastHeight, Falloff, ShowArea, ConeAngle, ManaPerSecond); `GBSpellString::EffectPrefix`; `AGBSpell_Shield::GetShieldHealth()`, `ComputeBlockedDamage`; `AGBSpell_Enchant::MakeEffectId`, `ComputeDurationScale`; spellbook `HandleQTEFinished(const FGBQTEResult&, FName)` (payload order of `CreateUObject`).
- The spellbook cancels its sustained spell itself on weapon switch and on death.
- A blocking ice wall is a Neutral actor with attributes using the `BlockAllDynamic` profile (object type WorldDynamic).
- Not verified: `IsValid(TObjectPtr)` implicit conversion.
- Tests: `Glyphbound.Spells.ResolveScaling`, `ResolveNoQTE`, `DamageInfo`.

### ARCHITECT DECISION (apply during integration): Neutral targets are damageable by everyone
The projectile overlaps WorldDynamic and ignores Neutral actors, so as written it would fly THROUGH the ice wall, and nothing could wear a wall down. Rule to implement:
1. `UGBCombatLibrary`: add `static bool CanDamage(const AActor* Instigator, const AActor* Target)`: true when the target has attributes and is alive and (the instigator is null, OR either team is Neutral, OR the teams are hostile). `DealDamage` uses it (still honoring `bAllowFriendlyFire`). `DealRadialDamage` uses it too. So Player and Enemy never hurt their own team, and Neutral things (spell walls, future destructibles) can be hurt by anyone. `AreHostile` keeps its meaning (Player vs Enemy only) for AI targeting and for spell area effects that should only touch enemies.
2. `AGBProjectile`: a valid target is anything `CanDamage` accepts except the instigator itself; a projectile that touches a Neutral actor with attributes damages it and stops (no pierce through walls).
3. Spell area behaviors (wall burn, zone, orb, beam, trap) keep using hostile-only gathering, so the player's fire wall does not burn the player's ice wall. Leave them as they are.
EOF

# Turns file-local anonymous namespaces into named ones and qualifies every use after the block,

set -e

tool_input.content:
# Code review: Glyphbound day 1 (read-only)

You are the second-opinion reviewer for **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter in Unreal Engine 5.9.0 (C++), made for a 4-day game jam. Do not modify any file. Do not build or run anything.

## Context
- Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (short). Design is in `Design/GDD.md` (sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 matter most).
- Code: `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/` (about 17,000 lines, written today by ten AI implementers in parallel against header contracts, then being compiled by another agent right now, so a missing include is NOT what we want from you).
- Data: `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`, loaded by `Data/GBDataSubsystem.cpp` into the structs of `Data/GBDataTypes.h`.
- Engine source for checking APIs: `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source`.

## What to look for (real defects only, in this priority order)
1. **Runtime bugs in the combat core**: `Combat/`, `Stats/`, `Weapons/`, `Spells/` (damage path, status effects, projectile collisions and lifetimes, ammo and reload state, cooldowns, mana spent / refunded wrongly, sustained spells never ending, time dilation left on after the QTE).
2. **Mismatches between data and code**: a stat, param, string key, id, enum value or class path used in a JSON file that the code never reads or spells differently (and the reverse: code reading a key no JSON defines, so it silently falls back to a default). Check ids across files (spells, weapons, items, status effects, enemies, encounters, sprites, skills modifier keys like `Spell.Fireball.ExplosionRadius`).
3. **Cross-module contract breaks**: one module assuming something another does not do (initialization order in `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.cpp` BeginPlay, who restores health on era travel, who saves checkpoints, who closes the death menu, delegate bindings never removed, objects kept alive only by raw pointers and collected by the GC, `TWeakObjectPtr` not checked).
4. **Things that work in the Editor but break in a packaged build**: editor-only APIs outside guards, assets loaded by path at runtime that the cook would not include (see `Glyphbound/Config/DefaultGame.ini`), transient textures, `LoadClass` paths.
5. **Logic errors in the QTE** (`QTE/GBQTELogic.cpp`, `QTE/GBQTEComponent.cpp`): scoring, time limit in real time, input routed while inactive.
6. **Violations of the project rule "no gameplay numbers in code"** only when it is a real balance value (damage, cost, cooldown, speed, duration) hardcoded where data should decide.

Do not report: style, naming, formatting, missing comments, micro-optimizations, hypothetical multiplayer issues (the game is single player), or anything about tests being too few.

## Output format
A numbered list, most severe first, at most 30 items. For each:
- `file:line` (or lines),
- what is wrong, in one or two sentences,

# Code review: Glyphbound day 1 (read-only)

You are the second-opinion reviewer for **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter in Unreal Engine 5.9.0 (C++), made for a 4-day game jam. Do not modify any file. Do not build or run anything.

## Context
- Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (short). Design is in `Design/GDD.md` (sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 matter most).
- Code: `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/` (about 17,000 lines, written today by ten AI implementers in parallel against header contracts, then being compiled by another agent right now, so a missing include is NOT what we want from you).
- Data: `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`, loaded by `Data/GBDataSubsystem.cpp` into the structs of `Data/GBDataTypes.h`.
- Engine source for checking APIs: `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source`.

## What to look for (real defects only, in this priority order)
1. **Runtime bugs in the combat core**: `Combat/`, `Stats/`, `Weapons/`, `Spells/` (damage path, status effects, projectile collisions and lifetimes, ammo and reload state, cooldowns, mana spent / refunded wrongly, sustained spells never ending, time dilation left on after the QTE).
2. **Mismatches between data and code**: a stat, param, string key, id, enum value or class path used in a JSON file that the code never reads or spells differently (and the reverse: code reading a key no JSON defines, so it silently falls back to a default). Check ids across files (spells, weapons, items, status effects, enemies, encounters, sprites, skills modifier keys like `Spell.Fireball.ExplosionRadius`).
3. **Cross-module contract breaks**: one module assuming something another does not do (initialization order in `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.cpp` BeginPlay, who restores health on era travel, who saves checkpoints, who closes the death menu, delegate bindings never removed, objects kept alive only by raw pointers and collected by the GC, `TWeakObjectPtr` not checked).
4. **Things that work in the Editor but break in a packaged build**: editor-only APIs outside guards, assets loaded by path at runtime that the cook would not include (see `Glyphbound/Config/DefaultGame.ini`), transient textures, `LoadClass` paths.
5. **Logic errors in the QTE** (`QTE/GBQTELogic.cpp`, `QTE/GBQTEComponent.cpp`): scoring, time limit in real time, input routed while inactive.
6. **Violations of the project rule "no gameplay numbers in code"** only when it is a real balance value (damage, cost, cooldown, speed, duration) hardcoded where data should decide.

Do not report: style, naming, formatting, missing comments, micro-optimizations, hypothetical multiplayer issues (the game is single player), or anything about tests being too few.

## Output format
A numbered list, most severe first, at most 30 items. For each:
- `file:line` (or lines),
- what is wrong, in one or two sentences,
- why it matters when playing (what the player would see),
- the smallest fix you would make.

## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
The owner asked the architect not to stop for missing design details. Everything below was chosen so the prototype could be built; **all of it is provisional** and waits for the owner's word. Numbers are in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and can be changed there without touching code.

### Rules
- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.
- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.
- **Swapping weapons:** picking up a gun or a staff replaces the one held; the old one is left on the floor. A gun that is picked up comes fully loaded.
- **Reload:** the bullets left in the old magazine are lost (classic tactical style). A gun reloads by itself when its magazine runs dry. Ammo pickups give one spare magazine, up to the gun's maximum.
- **Sustained spells (flamethrower, ice shield):** after the QTE they run for their Duration, or until the same spell key is pressed again, the weapon is switched, or the player dies. Mana is paid once, at the start.
- **Ice shield QTE:** part 1 (power) scales its duration and health; part 2 (reach) scales how much frontal damage it blocks.
- **Weapon enchant QTE:** part 1 scales how long the buff lasts; part 2 scales how strong it is. Only one enchant at a time. The enchanted gun deals the element's damage type and applies its effect on hit (fire burns, lightning shocks, ice chills).
- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it burns enemies that touch it. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.
- **QTE:** a wrong key consumes its step. A gesture is judged when the hand stops for a moment or the stroke is clearly complete. If both parts are fully missed the spell fizzles, and the mana is still spent and the cooldown still starts.
- **New spells** go to the first free loadout slot.
- **Elemental sword:** the hilt and the gems are not consumed when forging, so the player re-forges from the inventory to switch element.
- **Enemies:** once hit, an enemy chases the player from any distance. Enemies of the other era are frozen and hidden, not simulated.
- **Encounters:** if the player dies during one, its living enemies are removed and it starts again from wave 1 on return. Progress flags are never rolled back.
- **Checkpoints:** saved at the start, on every era travel, on entering a checkpoint zone and when an encounter is cleared. Death brings back the player's state as it was at the checkpoint (health, mana, ammo, items, spells, skills).
- **Consumables** can be used at full health or mana (they are wasted).
- **Art rule on pickups:** cyberpunk items (injection, grenade, magazine, sword hilt) lie on the floor as 3D shapes; medieval ones (potions, gems, books, staffs) as pixel-art sprites.

payload.last_assistant_message:
El día 1 está cerrado: Glyphbound compila, pasa 22 tests y queda empaquetado en `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` (245 MB). **Nadie lo ha jugado todavía.** Lo verifiqué compilando, con los tests y con una prueba automática que arranca el juego solo, usa los sistemas, saca capturas y sale; no es PIE. Esa prueba también pasa sobre el `.exe` empaquetado.

## Qué hay en el build
- **Jugador:** primera persona con salto, doble salto y dash, vida y maná con regeneración, y los controles del GDD §9.
- **Armas:** bastón con ataque básico y pistola con cambio entre ambos; escopeta, rifle y espada ya existen como datos. Manos en pixel art.
- **Hechizos:** los 13 del GDD, sobre 8 comportamientos reutilizables. Cada parámetro tiene base, mínimo, máximo y qué parte del QTE lo escala.
- **QTE:** primera versión, con secuencia de teclas, gesto y límite de 3 s; se apaga con `gb.QTE 0`.
- **Eras:** arena de prueba hecha en código, con portal y fundido, una sala que solo abre en el futuro y una rampa que aparece al limpiar la oleada del pasado.
- **Adelantado de los días 2 y 3:** enemigos y oleadas, inventario con consumibles y recetas, los dos árboles de habilidades, HUD en dos estilos, checkpoints y muerte.

Todos los números están en `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` y se pueden cambiar con un editor de texto, incluso en el build empaquetado (`gb.ReloadData` los recarga en partida).

## Decisiones que tomé
- **Sin GAS.** Lo sustituyen un sistema de estadísticas con modificadores, una única función de daño y un componente de efectos de estado.
- **C++ puro y sin assets binarios.** Mapa, controles y sprites provisionales se generan desde texto, así que todo queda en git.
- **Reparto del trabajo.** Escribí yo las cabeceras (los contratos); diez subagentes Opus en High las implementaron en paralelo; Muse Spark hizo la integración y las correcciones; Codex Sol 6.1 Medium revisó.
- **Morir no quita nada de lo recogido.** Vuelves al checkpoint con vida, maná y munición llenos. Lo cambié porque la revisión mostró que, con la regla anterior, una muerte podía borrar recompensas para siempre.
- **Reglas y números provisionales.** Todo lo que tuve que inventar está en la sección 18 del GDD, para que lo confirmes o lo cambies.

## Qué falló por el camino
- **Arena sin construir.** El juego compilaba y pasaba tests y revisión, pero el jugador caía al vacío; lo detectó la prueba automática.
- **Sprites en magenta.** Las claves de color distinguían mayúsculas y Unreal no; corregido.
- **Empaquetado.** Falló dos veces: por una función que solo existe en el Editor y por un plugin que yo había desactivado (Cascade). Ambos corregidos.
- **Revisión de Codex.** Encontró 9 defectos reales, todos corregidos. Cuatro de esos arreglos tocan colisiones e IA y solo están comprobados leyendo el código.
- **Plugins.** Apagar 102 no aceleró el arranque en caliente del Editor (10–11 s antes y después).

## Qué necesito de ti
Juega el zip y apunta lo que notes, sobre todo:
- sensación del movimiento y del dash;
- velocidad del ratón y si el QTE reconoce los gestos;
- si los disparos aciertan a los enemigos y cuentan los tiros a la cabeza;
- si el muro de hielo bloquea;

{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md","content":"## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.

| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS) |
| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
| **Ice** | Ice shield (held block, like a first-person RPG shield, but with a cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |

### Spell loadout
- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall.

### Learning the other spells: elemental zones
- The **medieval castle** has **elemental zones**, one per element.
- Each zone has a **challenge**: a wave, a sub-boss or a boss.
- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
- **Air passives** are learned the same way, in the air zone.
- The spell tree then upgrades what the player knows.
- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
- Keys: see §9.

### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
- **Only usable with a gun in hand** (it enchants the gun).
- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.

### General
- Spells cost **mana**.
- **Health and mana regenerate on their own** (potions and the injection speed it up). **No stamina.**
- Numbers for each spell (damage, cost, cooldowns, upgrade tiers): **TBD**, given later.
- The ice shield's exact limits (duration, damage absorbed, break behavior): **TBD**.

## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event

# Game Design Document (working draft)

> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
> Status: **v0.13, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.

## Changelog
- v0.13 (2026-11-12): architect's day-1 technical decisions recorded in 0.1 (C++ only, no GAS, JSON data, code-built test arena, canvas HUD); new section 18 lists every provisional rule and number the architect had to pick. Code structure in `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- v0.12 (2026-11-12): architect autonomy on every technical decision; iteration time is a priority (see `CLAUDE.md`).
- v0.11 (2026-11-12): the 3 s QTE limit covers the whole QTE.
- v0.10 (2026-11-12): QTE lasts 3 s and the player keeps moving in the direction they were moving; CENTRAL has an NVIDIA RTX 4080 Laptop GPU, so DLSS can be tested here.
- v0.9 (2026-11-12): code name Glyphbound; pixel-art look defined (3D geometry with low-res textures, 8-angle sprites); new §0.1 technical direction (C++, placeholders, PIE rule, data tables, travel fade, checkpoint-only saving, single player, size budget, NVIDIA award); camera locked during the QTE.
- v0.8 (2026-11-12): enemies do not respawn; provisional game order; story questions parked; open questions narrowed to what the prototype and base systems need.
- v0.7 (2026-11-12): full story (the entity, the false voice, the Valkyrie); elemental zones in the castle unlock the rest of each element; air passives learned the same way; shotgun and rifle dropped by enemies; era travel restores everything (bonfire-like); remaining keys confirmed.
- v0.6 (2026-11-12): art rule clarified for characters (style of the world they belong to); story premise; opening sequence with the first gun; starting spells; enchant only with a gun in hand; key changes (F quick-use, G interact, L1 enchant on gamepad); counter-style ammo refilled on era travel; automatic checkpoints; no sprint; one full-armor slot.
- v0.5 (2026-11-12): sword is a third slot; magazines, reload, limited ammo dropped by enemies; health and mana regenerate, no stamina; state carries across eras; checkpoints; one skill point pool; controls filled in; opening sequence; armor from chests; difficulty = hard only for now.
- v0.4 (2026-11-12): weapon skill tree contents; two held slots (one gun + one staff) and how to switch; no spells with a gun except the enchant; enchant key; air passives always on; ice shield QTE; staffs from chests; sword blade is pixel art with a medieval HUD; final boss mixes both styles.
- v0.3 (2026-11-12): art rule follows the object; the player is always pixel art; 5-spell loadout and controls; staffs and basic magic attack; gun aim; enchant has a QTE, player-chosen element, not on the sword; QTE grading and mana; two UI styles (90s RPG vs. modern cyberpunk) for HUD and skill trees.
- v0.2 (2026-11-12): theme reading, art rule, shared map with era-gated zones, cross-era style mixing, QTE = power + reach, weapon enchant spell, skill points from encounters, enemy waves and sub-bosses, no early melee, architect definition.
- v0.1 (2026-11-12): first dump of the owner's pitch.
